referees.quote: I do not think current work along b axis is conclusive for identifying the superconductivity gap of UTe2. I mean if the gap is nodal along a axis, the full gap along b axis seems not that important.
I cannot recommend publication of the paper in its present state... Several crucial points need to be checked (starting with the Wiedemann-Franz law) in order to strengthen the experimental analysis.
I do think the manuscript should eventually be published in this journal, however there are several issues I think should be addressed first.

note: No transfer from another journal is indicated; Version 0 is the first round. R1 is a borderline inference. Apart from the central objection, R1 asked only for two text corrections, so 'minor revision' is also defensible. 'Reject' was chosen because the referee disputes that the central claim is conclusive. R1's round-2 remark 'I'm not against the publication' fits initial reluctance. R2's first-round report is blank in the reviewer-comments section. Their recommendation comes from the report as quoted in the authors' first rebuttal. R2 requested further Wiedemann-Franz checks and more quantitative theory comparison. R3 asked for a zoomed inset, softer zero-field claims and label fixes.
